 Wyoming at UNC: TV info, stats, scouting Cowboys, notes and lineup combinations
 R.L. Bynum November 8, 2026 November 10, 2026 Basketball , Men's basketball 
 Post navigation
 Previous Next 
 By R.L. Bynum 
 Wyoming (2–0) at North Carolina (2–0) 
 When: 7 p.m. Tuesday
 Where: Smith Center
 Officials: Pat Driscoll, Jerry Heater and Brent Hampton
 TV: ACC Network | Anish Shroff play-by-play, Terrence Oglesby analyst
 Radio: Tar Heel Sports Network ( affiliates list ; streams on the Varsity Network app ) | Jones Angell play-by-play, Tyler Zeller analyst.
 Coaches: Wyoming coach Sundance Wicks (third season, 30–35) and UNC coach Michael Malone (first college head-coaching season, 2–0; 510–394 in NBA regular-season games, 44–36 in NBA playoff games)
 Series: UNC won the only meeting. That was a 90–74 Carolina win in the second round of the 2003 NIT at the Smith Center, when Melvin Scott scored a career-high 20 points and Raymond Felton had 14 assists, a UNC freshman record, for Coach Matt Doherty’s team.
 Opening results: UNC beat Western Carolina 80–72 on Nov. 2 and Wofford 109–70 on Friday at the Smith Center. Wyoming beat Division II Regis 95–48 on Nov. 3 and Idaho State 93–62 on Friday, both at home.
 Exhibition results: UNC beat Southern Cal 88–70 on Oct. 9 in Greensboro, lost 76–58 at Indiana on Oct. 18 and beat Charlotte 89–82 in overtime on Oct. 27. Wyoming beat Northern Colorado 94–68 on Oct. 11 in Gillette, Wyo., lost 89–76 to TCU on Oct. 17 in Midland, Texas, and beat College of Idaho 76–61 on Oct. 24 in Laramie.
 Projected Wyoming starters
 No. 3 | G | Khaden Bennett (top photo) | 6–4, 207 | senior Quinnipiac transfer 
— Led Wyoming with 15 points and added six rebounds and three assists against Regis, hitting a 3-pointer against his younger brother, Regis freshman Bryce Bennett, early in the first half.
— Started 32 of 33 games last season, averaging 10.2 points, 4.9 rebounds (tied for the team high) and 2.8 assists. He scored a career-high 27 points against Nevada, including 18 before halftime, and made six 3-pointers.
 No. 2 | G | Naz Meyer | 6–7, 202 | sophomore 
— Preseason All-Mountain West selection who had 18 points and nine rebounds against Idaho State, after scoring 11 points against Regis and 24 in the exhibition loss to TCU.
— Scored 27 points at Nevada last season as a freshman.
 No. 11 | F | Gavin Gores | 6–10, 230 | sophomore 
— Had 10 points and five rebounds against Regis, including a two-handed dunk during a 22–2 run. Against Idaho State, he opened the second half with a three-point play and a dunk to start a 9–0 run.
— Wicks on his consistency after the Regis win: “You’ve got to be the same guy every game.”
 No. 22 | G | Parker Gerrits | 6–2, 186 | junior Washington State transfer 
— Scored a career-high 12 points on 4-of-5 shooting in his Wyoming debut against Regis. Wicks has compared him to recent Cowboys “glue guys” Cole Henry and Kiani Saxon.
 No. 6 | G | Canin Jefferson | 6–2, 177 | senior North Alabama transfer 
— Had a team-high four assists and nine points against Regis.
 Other key Cowboys
 No. 10 | F | Renars Sondors | 6–9, 214 | junior ULM transfer 
— Scored 14 points off the bench against Idaho State, going 4-for-7 on 3-pointers, with three 3s and nine points before halftime.
 No. 19 | C | Linus Ruf | 6–11, 235 | freshman 
— Scored 10 points against Regis.
 No. 1 | F | Mike Mora | 6–6, 225 | junior Cal State Monterey Bay transfer 
— Scored 10 points on 4-of-7 shooting in his Wyoming debut against Regis.
 No. 5 | G | Madden Smiley | 6–4, 184 | freshman 
— The two-time Colorado 5A Player of the Year at Windsor High had a team-high eight rebounds in 21 minutes against Regis, then led Wyoming with eight points in the second half against Idaho State.
 Other newcomers: Kelan Gruver (freshman walk-on and Kansas 5A Player of the Year, who hit a 3-pointer with 1:35 left against Idaho State), Chris Pohl, Mattia De Martin and Micah Curtis. Returners Uriyah Rojas and Neil Summers are also on the roster.

 Three keys for Tar Heels
 — Finish defensive possessions. Wyoming grabbed 21 offensive rebounds against Idaho State and leads the country in offensive rebounding percentage (63.6%) through two games (with the strong caveat that this is against Division II Regis and Idaho State). Sayon Keita and Jarin Stevenson need to make first contact inside, and Carolina’s guards have to help on long rebounds. A clean rebound also gives Terrence Brown a chance to push the pace. 
— Keep Wyoming’s steals from becoming easy points. The Cowboys averaged 11.5 steals in their first two games, while Carolina committed only 8.5 turnovers per game. Brown and Neo Avdalas can keep that edge by giving each other clear outlets and making the simple pass when Wyoming crowds the ball. A live-ball turnover gives the Cowboys a chance to score before UNC can set its defense.
— Make Naz Meyer and Khaden Bennett score over a set defense. Naz Meyer (14.5 points per game) and Khaden Bennett (14.0) lead Wyoming in scoring. Carolina needs to keep them out of the middle and contest without sending extra help on every drive. That lets UNC stay closer to Renars Sondors, who has made a team-high five 3-pointers in two games.
 Notes
 — This will be the 600th UNC game at the Smith Center. UNC is 509–90, including 243–18 against non-conference teams.
— Carolina has won 20 straight home games. It’s the 10th-longest home winning streak in program history.
— This is the third of six consecutive home games to open the season, the first such stretch in program history.
— Wyoming finished 18–15 (9–11 Mountain West) in Coach Sundance Wicks ’ second season and lost 74–70 at Wichita State in the first round of the NIT. It was the program’s first postseason trip since the 2003 NIT, which ended with the loss at the Smith Center. League coaches picked the Cowboys fifth this season, behind New Mexico, Grand Canyon, Nevada and UNLV.
— Wicks is a Gillette, Wyo., native who was a Wyoming assistant under Jeff Linder , when the Cowboys reached the NCAA tournament in 2021, and spent one season as Green Bay’s head coach before returning in 2024.
— Wicks said Wyoming has to “integrate 10 new guys” after returning only five players: Khaden Bennett, Naz Meyer, Gavin Gores, Uriyah Rojas and Neil Summer s.
— Wicks after the Regis win: “That was the hardest I’ve seen our guys play in the preseason, up until now. We didn’t play that hard in the first three games in the exhibition season. We played hard.”
— Said Wicks in a story on the Wyoming athletics website : “It’s an NCAA tournament game for us. This is the way I look at it. You don’t get any of these opportunities. Nobody schedules this stuff anymore, so I’m grateful for the opportunity, I’m grateful that they scheduled us and they allowed us to play this game. It’s just like anybody right now, all these mid-majors are still trying to prove that we belong.”
— In the same story, the Wyoming writer calls the Smith Center “a living, breathing basketball museum.”
— Wyoming has outscored its two opponents 188–110. It shot 55% against Regis and held the Rangers to 38%, then held Idaho State to 31%.
— The rebounding numbers favor the Cowboys. Wyoming outrebounded Regis 41–23 and Idaho State 50–27, a combined 91–50 margin. Carolina was outrebounded 41–32 by Western Carolina, then won the battle against Wofford but allowed 17 offensive rebounds. UNC still had a 19–10 edge in second-chance points.
— Wyoming forced 33 turnovers in its two wins (19 against Regis and 14 against Idaho State) and scored 51 points off them (26 and 25). The Cowboys had 23 fast-break points against Regis and a 19–2 fast-break edge against Idaho State.
— Wicks on his team’s playing style: “We play really good on a flow. We trust guys to make decisions. Guys have worked all summer long to become solid, sound decision makers, not hero passers. Just easy-assist passers.”
— Twelve Cowboys scored against Idaho State, and Wyoming got 43 bench points against Regis.
— UNC center Cameron Fens , who is still ineligible, faced Wyoming twice while at South Dakota. On Dec. 10, 2024, he had eight points, seven rebounds and four blocks in South Dakota’s 82–81 home win. On Dec. 9, 2025, he had no points and two rebounds in South Dakota’s 106–79 loss at Wyoming.
— UNC’s 109 points against Wofford were the most since a 113–96 win over N.C. State on Feb. 5, 2019, and its first 100-point game since Nov. 15, 2024. The Tar Heels’ 58 bench points were the most since 2018. Carolina shot 52.1%, held Wofford to 33.3%, had 18 assists to eight turnovers and outscored the Terriers 20–4 on the fast break.
— Five Tar Heels scored in double figures against Wofford: Terrence Brown (21), Jaydon Young (15), Alex Samodurov (13), Maxi Adams (11) and Jarin Stevenson (10). Adams had 11 points and 11 rebounds for his first college double-double in his second game, and Samodurov had 13 points and seven rebounds in 18 minutes after not making an impact in the first four games.
— UNC is 23rd in the country in turnovers with 8.5 per game.
